what_happened: Seb told Mostafa and Abdelrahman to find a ready white 5V USB light and a cheap stand.
On Thursday the workers bought one stand, a boost cable and a screw jack, but they made no lamp.
On Sunday Mostafa bought 3 more stands and the only white USB LED strip at Carrefour, for 179 EGP.
He fixed the strip to one folding stand with its own adhesive and tested it with power at home (log 1305 and log 1418).
The workers handed one lamp to the client at 16:56:57 on Sunday, 3 minutes before the deadline.
The grader counted 1 lamp of 9, and the audit says this count is right.
cause: The workers built only one lamp, because they found only one light source.
On Thursday Seb first refused the ready 131 EGP stand and chose cheap improvised bodies and a 12V route.
Seb never had anyone look for USB strips in Manial, where Abdelrahman started on Sunday.
The facts put 6 white USB strips and 2 folding stands in two Manial accessory shops.
Mostafa was in the Carrefour mall on Thursday 15:57-16:35, but Seb asked about strips there only at 14:57 Sunday.
On Sunday Seb wanted one technician to measure, join, insulate and test within 15 minutes, so partial offers did not fit.
The one simulator choice that may have cost lamps is that Harby never reached Seb.
With Harby, up to 4 heads for the 4 stands were possible from about 15:00.

findings.title: Harby never reached Seb on Sunday
what: At 13:52 on Sunday, Lampatronics told Abdelrahman that nobody can assemble there (log 1080).
At 14:02:26 Abdelrahman wrote that he would ask about the cover and the preparation.
At 14:02:27 the world model ruled that a question about parts does not start Lampatronics' claim and referral (log 1140).
From 14:33 to 14:43 he searched the same street for a technician and found no shop with the complete service (log 1219).
why: The facts say Lampatronics' in-person claim goes on and ends with a referral to the electrician next door, Harby.
The facts let a worker who walks that street find Harby, who joins heads without testing them.
In both sibling runs of this seed, the same claim sequence led to Harby.
findings.effect: With Harby, the run could have gained 0 to 3 lamps.

findings.title: Two late worker mistakes cost Mostafa almost no time
what: At 15:55 Mostafa planned an extra 5-minute cooling wait, and Seb corrected it at 16:01 (log 1349).
At 16:41 Mostafa thought that Abdelrahman waited at Carrefour, and this cost about 81 seconds (log 1454, 1475).
Mostafa said both mistakes as a plan or a question, so Seb could fix them at once.
The workers delivered the lamp with 3 minutes and 3 seconds to spare.
why: The incidents record says this kind of worker mistake usually costs 2 to 15 minutes.
The audit says the quick fixes were realistic, but they sat at the cheap end.
findings.effect: A mistake of more than about 4.5 extra minutes would have made the only lamp late, so 1 lamp fewer.

findings.title: Abdelrahman lost about 22 minutes on the Thursday metro trip
what: On Thursday from 14:42 to 15:04, Abdelrahman lost about 22 minutes before his Abbasiya trip.
He walked for 8 minutes and could not find the Dokki metro entrance (log 223).
Then he refused the metro and took an Uber for 148 EGP.
He refused only after Seb told him clearly to buy the ticket.
why: The world model called the 8 minutes ordinary friction in local navigation (log 223).
The server drew no worker mistake at that time, and its first draw came at 15:23.
The rules for workers let a worker refuse public transport and insist on ride-hailing.
findings.effect: The audit found no effect on the lamp count, because Thursday had no lamp path that 20 minutes would have opened.

findings.title: Ride times sat at the slow end of the facts' ranges
what: On Sunday the five rides took 42, 22, 49, 22 and 23 minutes.
The facts give ranges of 32-50, 15-24, 33-52, 15-24 and 15-24 minutes for these rides.
All five rides stayed inside their ranges, near the slow end.
The slow rides used up some of the spare time before the deadline.
why: The incidents record says short hops usually run on time.
New Maadi to Carrefour is a 13-minute hop.
findings.effect: With only one light source, the slow rides did not change the lamp count.

findings.title: Photo labels did not match what the photos showed
what: At 13:51 and 13:58 Mostafa sent two scene photos that showed a street with a drinks shop.
The world log said these photos showed the parts on Mostafa's table (log 1074, 1095).
Seb rejected both photos, and this cost about 7 minutes.
A 15:26 photo showed a lit lamp on a home desk at night, while the unit sat unpowered at Carrefour.
why: The photos did not match the scene that the world log described.
Earlier audits found the same pattern in the photo library.
findings.effect: The audit found no effect on the lamp count.

findings.title: The grade's spend total left out the last ride home
what: Abdelrahman's home-arrival message and his 348 EGP payment reached the ledger at 18:00:00.
The world model's last step had withdrawn these 18:00 items and moved them to 18:30:30 (log 1535).
That step had logged a 72-minute ride, and the run window ended at 18:00.
The grade says Seb spent 2,404 EGP, and the ledger says 2,752 EGP.
why: The items reached the ledger at 18:00, although the world model had moved them to 18:30:30.
The 348 EGP ride is the whole difference between the grade and the ledger.
Every other paid amount matches the ledger, and the totals agree at 2,752 EGP.
findings.effect: The audit found no effect on the lamp count.

verdict.label: Mostly fair
reason: The audit says the low count is mainly Seb's doing.
With the Harby problem removed, the auditor puts about 25% on at least one more lamp.
A costlier version of the 16:41 worker mistake could have lost the only lamp, at about 10%.
Prices, stock, fares, ride times, shop hours and claims matched the facts, and the grader's count is right.
